question: Who has coined the term 'ecology'?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Ernst Haeckel**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **ecology **was **coined by **the **German zoologist Ernst Haeckel**.
 
• He was **an evolutionist **who was a strong proponent of **Darwinism **and who **proposed new notions **of the **evolutionary descent of human beings**.
 
• The **concept of environment **includes both other **organisms **and **physical surroundings**.
 
• It **involves relationships between individuals **within a **population **and **between individuals **of **different populations**.
 
• These interactions between individuals, between populations, and between organisms and their environment form ecological systems, or **ecosystems**.
 
• **Ecology **has been defined variously as **“the study of the interrelationships of organisms with their environment and each other,” “the economy of nature**,” and “the **biology of ecosystems.”**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Eugen Warming **was a **Danish botanist **and a **main founding figure **of the **scientific discipline of ecology**. Warming **wrote the first textbook **on **plant ecology**, taught the **first university course in ecology, **and gave the concept its meaning and content. 
 
• **Charles Robert Darwin **was an **English naturalist, geologist, and biologist**, best known for his contributions to evolutionary biology. His proposition that **all species of life have descended from a common ancestor **is **now widely accepted **and **considered a fundamental concept in science**.
 
• **Eugene Pleasants Odum **was an **American biologist **at the **University of Georgia **known for his pioneering work on ecosystem ecology. He and his brother Howard T. Odum wrote the popular **ecology textbook, Fundamentals of Ecology**.
